newsitem.title: USA: Fashion king Versace slain in Miami; hit suspected.
newsitem.headline: Fashion king Versace slain in Miami; hit suspected.

text.p: World-renowned fashion designer Gianni Versace was shot and killed on Tuesday in what police called a "targeted" murder in the tourist mecca of Miami Beach.
Police and witnesses said Versace, 50, was shot twice at point-blank range in the back of the head, execution-style, by a lone gunman who immediately fled the scene.
"I believe he was targeted, yes," Miami Beach Police Chief Richard Barreto told a news conference.
"There was apparently no robbery attempt involved."
Police were seeking a white man aged about 25 who approached Versace and shot him as he unlocked the gates of his lavish mansion shortly before 9 a.m. EDT (1300 GMT).

"The information that we now have suggests that this terrible crime was an extraordinary occurrence and not just a random robbery," Dade County Mayor Alex Penelas, who has jurisdiction over the several cities making up Greater Miami, told the news conference. He gave no other details.
Barreto said the Federal Bureau of Investigation was investigating but did not confirm a television report that FBI experts on contract killings had been brought in.
Barreto at first said a handgun was recovered near the scene but later declined to confirm the find.

Reporters saw police examining a black backpack like that carried by the killer. The pack was found a few blocks from the house. Television reports said clothing corresponding to that worn by the killer was later found abandoned in a parking garage near the murder site.

The Italian designer, 50, was returning to his home from a nearby restaurant on the glamorous Ocean Drive strip, a street of brightly painted art deco hotels and trendy restaurants featured in the Robin Williams movie "The Bird Cage."
Miami Beach, a narrow finger of land off the Florida mainland, is the centre of Miami's swinging fashion and music industry. It has its own police force and city administration.
Eddie Bianchi, 50, owner of a rollerblade shop, told Reuters he was nearby when the shooting occurred.
"We heard two shots. I saw people running. Gianni was on the stairs. He was shot twice in the head. We were trying to help Gianni on the floor, but we realised it was too late."
"Gianni Versace was a worldwide personality, so for the people who work here on Ocean Drive, it's really awful."
Behind police lines, a large bloodstain could be seen at the front of the mansion. Blood from Versace's wounds appeared to have spilled and poured down the stairs.
A single red rose, apparently left by a fan, lay on the sidewalk.
People at the scene said the white-haired Versace had walked to the nearby News Cafe, a popular 24-hour restaurant, to buy his morning paper and was shot upon his return home.

Globe-trotting Versace, who dressed some of the world's most beautiful women, was not a permanent resident of Miami Beach but frequently stayed at the white stone mansion, the only private residence on Ocean Drive.
Jason Binn, an editor at Ocean Drive magazine, said Versace would often walk unprotected along the streets of Miami Beach but was never bothered by fans.
"He was always the most giving person, he was always nice to people, it was never a scene, that's what he loved about Miami," he said.
A senior manager at the News Cafe said Versace was his usual gracious self when he walked to the shop to buy magazines Tuesday morning.
"There was nothing to detect any difference," Ryan Yorke told Reuters. Versace bought Newsweek, Entertainemnt Weekly, the New Yorker, People and American Books before leaving.
"He would come in the morning to get newspapers, sometimes he would have breakfast or lunch, most often alone but sometimes with five or six friends."

"He would hang out, relax, chill out, watch the parade on Ocean Drive. He didn't come here for business. He was always very gentle, unassuming, gracious, very private. We are all in a state of shock. The mood here is very sombre."
"He was a big player in bringing Miami Beach back to life."

The slaying recalled for many the murder of another Italian fashion czar, Maurizio Gucci, in Milan in 1995. His former wife and two alleged hit men were among five people charged in that killing in February this year.
